query_text: how do you type up minutes of a meeting

content.text:
Here’s a simple way to type up meeting minutes:

## 1. Start with the basic details

At the top, include:

**Meeting title:**  
**Date:**  
**Time:**  
**Location or platform:**  
**Chairperson/leader:**  
**Minute-taker:**  
**Attendees:**  
**Apologies/absent:**  

Example:

> **Staff Meeting Minutes**  
> **Date:** June 7, 2026  
> **Time:** 10:00 AM  
> **Location:** Conference Room / Zoom  
> **Chair:** Maria Lopez  
> **Minutes taken by:** James Carter  
> **Present:** Maria Lopez, James Carter, Priya Singh  
> **Apologies:** Daniel Kim

## 2. Follow the meeting agenda

Use the agenda as your structure. Each agenda item should have its own heading.

Example:

### 1. Welcome and introductions
The chair welcomed everyone and outlined the purpose of the meeting.

### 2. Review of previous minutes
The minutes from the previous meeting were reviewed and approved.

### 3. Project update
Priya reported that the project is on schedule. The team discussed possible delays with supplier delivery.

## 3. Record decisions, not every word

Minutes are usually a summary, not a transcript. Focus on:

- Main topics discussed
- Decisions made
- Actions agreed
- Who is responsible for each action
- Deadlines

Example:

> It was agreed that the marketing team will prepare a draft campaign plan by June 21, 2026.

## 4. Include action items clearly

A table works well:

| Action | Person responsible | Deadline |
|---|---:|---:|
| Prepare campaign draft | Marketing team | June 21, 2026 |
| Contact supplier about delivery dates | Priya Singh | June 14, 2026 |
| Circulate revised budget | James Carter | June 10, 2026 |

## 5. End with next meeting details

Include:

**Next meeting:**  
**Date:**  
**Time:**  
**Location:**  

Example:

> **Next meeting:** June 28, 2026, at 10:00 AM in the conference room.

## 6. Proofread and send them out

Before sharing the minutes:

- Check names and dates
- Make sure actions are clear
- Use consistent formatting
- Keep the language neutral and professional
- Send them to attendees soon after the meeting

## Simple meeting minutes template

```text
Meeting Minutes

Meeting title:
Date:
Time:
Location/platform:
Chairperson:
Minute-taker:

Present:
Apologies/absent:

1. Welcome
[Brief summary]

2. Approval of previous minutes
[Brief summary]

3. Matters arising
[Brief summary]

4. Agenda item one
[Discussion summary]
Decision:
Action:

5. Agenda item two
[Discussion summary]
Decision:
Action:

6. Any other business
[Brief summary]

Next meeting:
Date:
Time:
Location/platform:

Meeting closed at:
```

A good rule is: **write what was discussed, what was decided, and who needs to do what next.**
